description: Every DUI diagnostic DreamGUI can report. name is the EDreamUIDiagnosticCode entry; title is the first sentence of meaning, which is the documentation's; fix is given where the documentation has one (the layout codes); doc is the code on the documentation site.

stages.title: Lexer
stages.meaning: A character sequence that is not a token.

stages.title: Parser
stages.meaning: Tokens that do not form the grammar.

stages.title: Meaning
stages.meaning: Grammatical, but the tree does not hold together: a duplicate id, an unknown type.

stages.title: Values
stages.meaning: A value that does not fit the property it is written on.

stages.title: Building the tree
stages.meaning: Reflection refused the write, or the target object does not exist.

stages.title: Compiling
stages.meaning: The .dui could not be attached to its Blueprint.

stages.title: Write-back
stages.meaning: The designer's edit could not be put into the text.

stages.title: Layout
stages.meaning: A compiled screen, laid out at a viewport size, shows a problem. From DreamMCP's `layout` and `preview` only.

codes.name: UnexpectedCharacter
codes.title: A character that cannot begin any token.
codes.meaning: A character that cannot begin any token.

codes.name: UnterminatedString

codes.meaning: A string that reaches the end of its line without its closing quote.

codes.meaning: A `/*` that never reaches `*/`.

codes.meaning: A colour whose digit count is not 3, 4, 6 or 8.

codes.meaning: An asset path longer than an `FName` holds.

codes.name: UnexpectedToken

codes.meaning: A token where the grammar wants something else; the message names both.

codes.meaning: A `{` with no matching `}`.

codes.name: UnclosedTuple

codes.meaning: A `(` with no matching `)`.

codes.meaning: A property with no `=` or arrow, or nothing after it.

codes.meaning: No root node in a file compiled into a class, or more than one.

codes.name: MalformedClassDeclaration

codes.meaning: `class` twice, with an empty path, or inside a node.

codes.name: MalformedWasClause

codes.meaning: `@key(…)` holding something other than one string, or after a value that is not a string.

codes.meaning: A `for` / `each` header that is not `<keyword> Var in Source` or `Source()`.

codes.meaning: The right side of `<-`, `<->` or an `emit`'s arguments that do not parse.

codes.meaning: A `use` that could not be honoured: no such file, unreadable, does not parse, or a cycle.

codes.name: NestingTooDeep

codes.meaning: Blocks or parentheses nested deeper than 256.

codes.meaning: A `timeline` block or line that is not the grammar.

codes.name: MalformedUseDeclaration

codes.meaning: `use … as` without a name, a keyword as the name, or a class path without `as`.

codes.name: MalformedPropsBlock

codes.meaning: A `props` line that is not `Type Name` or `Type Name = value`, or `props` inside a node.

codes.meaning: An `events` entry that is not `Name` or `Name(Type Param, …)`, or `events` inside a node.

codes.name: MalformedConditional

codes.meaning: An `if` without its condition or block, an `else` with no `if`, or a branch holding something other than widgets.

codes.name: MalformedSlotDeclaration
codes.title: A slot with `default` twice, or a block that both declares and fills
codes.meaning: A slot with `default` twice, or a block that both declares and fills: a declaration holds components, properties, slot lines and `@tag` lines, and a fill holds widgets only (a `@tag` line beside them included).

codes.name: MalformedRows
codes.title: A `rows` table that does not read
codes.meaning: A `rows` table that does not read: a column list that is not names, a column twice, a row with the wrong number of values.

codes.name: MalformedViewModelsBlock
codes.title: A `viewmodels` line that is not `Type Name`, `= new`, `= global ["Name"]` or `= parent ["Name"]` (an empty `""` name included), or a `viewmodels` block inside a node.
codes.meaning: A `viewmodels` line that is not `Type Name`, `= new`, `= global ["Name"]` or `= parent ["Name"]` (an empty `""` name included), or a `viewmodels` block inside a node.

codes.name: MalformedTextAnnotation
codes.title: `@note(…)` not holding one string, `@max(…)` not one whole number of at least 1, either after a value that is not a string, an annotation written twice, or `@noloc` with `@key`, `@note` or `@max`.
codes.meaning: `@note(…)` not holding one string, `@max(…)` not one whole number of at least 1, either after a value that is not a string, an annotation written twice, or `@noloc` with `@key`, `@note` or `@max`.

codes.name: MalformedContainer
codes.title: A list (`[a, b]`) or a map (`{ key
codes.meaning: A list (`[a, b]`) or a map (`{ key: value }`) that does not read: a bracket never closed, two elements with no comma between them, or a map entry that is not `key: value`. A struct's first entry may go without a key.

codes.name: MalformedTag
codes.title: A `@tag` line that does not read
codes.meaning: A `@tag` line that does not read: nothing after `@tag`, a number or a string, two names with no comma between them, a trailing comma. Also a `@tag` line in a `style`, or directly in a `for` / `each` body.

codes.meaning: With DreamLoc in the project: a language's translation of a text, laid out in the text, is cut or runs past its box.

codes.name: TranslationGlyphsMissing

codes.meaning: With DreamLoc in the project: a language's translation of a text has characters no face of the text's font has.

codes.meaning: A designer edit with no home in the file: an unknown node, a bound property, a slot with no block.

codes.meaning: The file changed under a pending edit; nothing was written.

codes.name: PatchValueNotRepresentable

codes.meaning: A value the language cannot spell (a non-finite number); its line is left alone.

codes.name: PatchSyntaxNotWritable

codes.meaning: An edit to something no line spells: a visibility an `if` decides, a shorthand that cannot be rewritten, a change to `Tags` that no line can take (written both ways, or a name an `@tag` line cannot hold).

codes.name: PatchStyleComponentNotWritable
codes.title: An edit to a value a style's `+` line gives the node, from a caller that writes no override.
codes.meaning: An edit to a value a style's `+` line gives the node, from a caller that writes no override. The designer writes it as a `+` line on the node instead; a script can add that line, or change the style.

codes.name: LayoutOffScreen
codes.title: What can show of a node reaches more than 1 px past an edge of the viewport, or lies wholly outside it
codes.meaning: What can show of a node reaches more than 1 px past an edge of the viewport, or lies wholly outside it; or a text that does not fit its box spills off the screen where nothing clips it. A clipped part does not count; one finding per branch. Most often: a fixed `AnchoredPosition` measured from the centre, or a box with more children than room.
codes.fix: anchor the node to the edge it belongs to (`AnchorMin`/`AnchorMax`/`Pivot` 0 or 1) and keep its position small; or give the box room

codes.name: LayoutTextOverflow
codes.title: A text cut short by its overflow policy, or laid out past its box
codes.meaning: A text cut short by its overflow policy, or laid out past its box; the message gives the size it needs and the box it has. Most often: a fixed `SizeDelta` too small for the words; a text in a box that gives it no width.
codes.fix: a bigger box, `@slot SizeRule = Auto`, `WrapTextAt = <the width you want>`, or a smaller `FontSize`

codes.name: LayoutTooSmall
codes.title: A node that draws or can be pressed under 1 px wide or high (an info for a plain widget with children), or a pressable control under 24 x 24 px.
codes.meaning: A node that draws or can be pressed under 1 px wide or high (an info for a plain widget with children), or a pressable control under 24 x 24 px. Most often: a node with no `SizeDelta` and point anchors; a button sized by its content only.
codes.fix: `AnchorData.SizeDelta = (w, h)`, anchors that stretch, `MinDesiredSize`; buttons at least 24 x 24 px (48 px tall reads well)

codes.name: LayoutOverlappingControls
codes.title: Two pressable controls in one canvas overlapping on the screen by 2 px or more on both axes, wherever they are in the tree
codes.meaning: Two pressable controls in one canvas overlapping on the screen by 2 px or more on both axes, wherever they are in the tree: a press there reaches only the upper one. A small control lying on one four times its area or more is layered on purpose and not reported. Most often: positions written by hand.
codes.fix: put them in a `+ VerticalBox`/`+ HorizontalBox` with `Spacing`

codes.name: LayoutNearlyAligned
codes.title: Siblings whose left, right, top or bottom edges or centres differ by more than 0.5 and at most 3 px, or a row or column of three or more whose gaps do.
codes.meaning: Siblings whose left, right, top or bottom edges or centres differ by more than 0.5 and at most 3 px, or a row or column of three or more whose gaps do. The plain visuals inside a box no bigger than 128 px (the parts of an icon drawn from shapes) are not compared. Most often: two hand-written positions or sizes a pixel or two apart.
codes.fix: give them the same value, or let one box align them

codes.name: LayoutBreaksAtSize
codes.title: DUI8001 to DUI8004, DUI8008 or DUI8009 at one of the further viewport sizes `layout` was given (`sizes`), and not at the first.
codes.meaning: DUI8001 to DUI8004, DUI8008 or DUI8009 at one of the further viewport sizes `layout` was given (`sizes`), and not at the first. Most often: fixed positions from the centre, fixed widths wider than the smaller screen.
codes.fix: anchors to edges, boxes that fill (`@slot SizeRule = Fill`), sizes that stretch

codes.name: LayoutLowContrast
codes.title: In `preview`
codes.meaning: In `preview`: a text's colour against the median of the pixels just inside its box, under 3 to 1 (WCAG's contrast ratio); an info under 4.5 to 1 for text under 24 px. Most often: text colour close to what is behind it.
codes.fix: a lighter text on a dark backdrop or the other way round, until the ratio is at least 4.5 to 1

codes.name: LayoutOutsideFrame
codes.title: A node that draws more than 4 px (and 5 % of its size) past the panel or card it sits in
codes.meaning: A node that draws more than 4 px (and 5 % of its size) past the panel or card it sits in: the nearest ancestor that draws a box, or the plate an overlay puts under it. What is measured is what it draws -- a text's glyphs, a shape's outline, a rect block's body. A node tagged `Bleed` (or inside one), a frame that clips, and a plate as large as its frame (a face over its shadow) are not reported. Most often: a child bigger than its card, or placed past its edge; a key label hung under its icon's slot.
codes.fix: make it smaller or move it in, or give the panel (or the slot) room; a glow or bleed meant to go past: `@tag Bleed`

codes.name: LayoutCoversText
codes.title: A visual that takes no pointer, drawn after a text in its canvas, over 12 % or more of its glyphs -- or a small decoration lying mostly in the text's line
codes.meaning: A visual that takes no pointer, drawn after a text in its canvas, over 12 % or more of its glyphs -- or a small decoration lying mostly in the text's line; or a text laid across the edge of a small shape drawn under it that is not its plate (a label slid onto the next badge), part of its letters on the shape and the rest off it. Its backplate (drawn before it and holding it), an outline with no body, a veil over the whole card and a scrim over most of the screen are not reported, nor a node tagged `Bleed`. Most often: an accent bar, a shape or a glow written after the text and overlapping it.
codes.fix: move it off the text, or write it before the text so it is drawn under it; a sheen meant to lie over it: `@tag Bleed`

codes.name: LayoutUnbalanced
codes.title: A panel whose content keeps to one side (a band of 38 % or more empty), leaves a wide band empty across its middle, or spreads its rows thin
codes.meaning: A panel whose content keeps to one side (a band of 38 % or more empty), leaves a wide band empty across its middle, or spreads its rows thin; cautious, and never along a bar or a sidebar. Most often: content in fixed positions at the top of a panel sized for more; rows spaced far apart.
codes.fix: let the content fill (`@slot SizeRule = Fill`, anchors that stretch), spread it out, or make the panel smaller
